newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end off, CVRD plummets.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end off, CVRD plummets.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended off 0.38 percent, with mining giant CVRD preferred plunging 8.09 percent to 25.55 reais, the worst performance among blue chips, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 48 most active stocks closed at 10,180 points. Volume was 546.6 million reais ($515.6 million).

Analysts said CVRD preferred fell amid disappointment that the company's privatization auction Tuesday did not draw a higher premium and the winning group was not the one headed by local industrial conglomerate Grupo Votorantim.
Traders had speculated that CVRD's 32.00 real final price, 20 percent above the firm's base price, could have been higher.

The market also had widely expected Votorantim's Valecom group to win the auction. Instead, the Valepar consortium, led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN, was the winning bidder of a 41.73 percent voting stake in CVRD.
Some analysts had said they preferred the Valecom group because it included major global mining companies.
CVRD common stock, in turn, ended flat at 28.90 reais, roughly where it has traded since April 28.
Other brokers, however, said the drop in CVRD preferred stock had more to do with pension funds, members of the winning CSN group, who sold shares to raise cash.
Despite CVRD preferred's weak performance, benchmark managed to prevent local shares from falling too sharply.
Telebras preferred rose 0.24 percent to 126.80 reais. Its common stock lost 0.09 percent to 117.40 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras fell 0.22 percent to 227 reais. Federal holding Eletrobras rose 1.0 percent to 505 reais.
Analysts said the market could remain weak on continued profit-taking amid worries over slow progress on the government's civil service reform bill in Congress.
